note: Controlled relation vocabulary. A relation outside this list is still allowed but must carry the quality_flag relation_unmapped, so an unmapped relation is visible to the reader instead of hidden in free text.

increases.description: subject raises the measured quantity of object

decreases.description: subject lowers the measured quantity of object

outperforms.description: subject achieves a better score than object under comparable conditions

underperforms.description: subject achieves a worse score than object

is_superior_to.description: qualitative superiority, use when no metric is named

correlates_with.description: statistical association without a causal claim

causes.description: intervention on subject changes object; only when the source asserts causality

requires.description: subject cannot hold unless object does

uses.description: subject employs object as a component, dataset or method

measures.description: subject is an instrument or metric reporting object

achieves.description: subject attains object as a result

extends.description: subject builds on object with added scope

contradicts.description: subject and object cannot both hold as stated

limits.description: subject constrains the scope of object

derives_from.description: provenance: subject is computed from object

direction_rules: increases/decreases name the quantity as object, not the model: 'top_k=2 increases throughput', not 'throughput increases top_k'
outperforms is directional: the better system is the subject, the reference is the object
correlates_with is symmetric, causes is not; swapping them changes the claim's truth value
when the source compares two systems without naming a metric, use is_superior_to and record the metric as a qualifier
